================================================================
corpus_hash_v1 (panel-locked T.10 freeze)
================================================================

  35c276c73a52d916daafda2598b215d73e7fd694d4a0673e34ac1ef948f5a4b7

Domain separator:   DSFB-GPU-ATLAS:LITERATURE-CORPUS:v1\0
Schema identifier:  DSFB-GPU-ATLAS:CORPUS-HASH-SCHEMA:v1
Compute path:       dsfb_gpu_atlas_corpus::corpus_hash::compute_corpus_hash_v1
                    (SHA-256 over the canonical-byte projection
                    of the live T.1-T.9 corpus material).

================================================================
Material projection (panel-locked sections, in canonical order)
================================================================

  Section A — SCHEMA + version strings.
  Section B — RECORDS: 54 canonical detector records, sorted by
              canonical_id ascending.
  Section C — COURT: 66 dedup-court decisions
              (52 canonical + 12 alias + 2 composition).
  Section D — ALIAS_CLAIMS: 12 T.4 first-batch alias claims,
              sorted by alias_id ascending.
  Section E — USEFULNESS: 54 ledger rows, sorted by triple
              (canonical_id, task_id, dataset_id).
  Section F — END terminator.

Per-record canonical bytes carry:
  - canonical_id (u32 BE)
  - display_name (length-prefixed UTF-8)
  - aliases (length + array of length-prefixed strings)
  - source_refs (length + array; each ref has citation_key /
    title / authors / year / venue_or_source / doi_or_url / notes)
  - origin_domains.0 (u16 BE — the domain bitset)
  - primitive_family.as_str() (length-prefixed wire name)
  - mathematical_form.as_str()
  - decision_functional.as_str()
  - input_requirements.0 (u32 BE)
  - output_witness.as_str()
  - witness_role.as_str()
  - negative_witness_kind.as_str()
  - fusion_axes.0 (u16 BE)
  - confuser_profile.as_str()
  - deterministic_status.as_str()
  - implementation_status.as_str()      (L-band)
  - gpu_family.as_str()
  - parameter_bounds.description
  - duplicate_group.0 (u32 BE)
  - genealogy (derived_from / generalizes / special_case_of /
    is_origin) — id arrays + boolean.
  - usefulness snapshot (7 fields, big-endian)
  - lifecycle_state.as_str()
  - constitution_compliance (8 booleans)

Per-court-decision canonical bytes carry:
  - subject (Canonical(c) or AliasClaim(a))
  - literature_name
  - decision (Canonical / AliasOf(c) / ParameterisationOf(c) /
    CompositionOf(ids) / StochasticOriginalDeterministicReduction(c) /
    RejectedNotDeterministic / RejectedNotDetector / DeferredNeedsReview)
  - reason_code wire name
  - notes string

Per-ledger-row canonical bytes carry:
  - canonical_id, task_id, domain, dataset_id (the triple key)
  - evidence_level.as_str()
  - lifecycle_state.as_str()
  - score_kind.as_str()
  - empirical fields (9 fields, big-endian)
  - ledger_source.as_str()
  - reason_code.as_str()

The hash is NOT over rendered TXT/JSON. Re-rendering the public
reports does NOT change the hash; mutating any T.1-T.9 payload
byte WILL change the hash.

================================================================
Detector ladder status (unchanged by T.10)
================================================================

  D16  -- CPU + GPU audit path (legacy).
  D64  -- CPU + GPU; R.13 ~55x full-pipeline campaign reduction
          headline at 256x4096 K=64.
  D128 -- CPU + GPU scaling-ladder proof (R.9.d.1).
  D205 -- CPU + GPU byte-equivalent (R.9.d.2 + R.9.d.2.1).
          GPU detector tree-digest hashes the full 264-byte wide
          stride; R.10b compact-pack for D205 is deferred.

D16/D64/D128/D205 registry hashes are unchanged by T.10.

================================================================
Explicit non-claims
================================================================

T.10 freezes corpus_hash_v1 and introduces a CaseFileV2 header
receipt. It does NOT:

  - Generate registry_hash_v2.
  - Emit the 2,000-detector Atlas registry.
  - Run Atlas family kernels on GPU.
  - Publish a corpus artifact externally.
  - Deposit anything to Zenodo / DOI registries.
  - Change the R.13 D64 headline.
  - Change any D16/D64/D128/D205 registry hash.
  - Make claims about empirical detector usefulness beyond the
    T.8 conservative seed.
  - Generate Atlas case-file episode transcripts (the
    CaseFileV2 body is a future commit; T.10 ships header
    receipt only).

================================================================
Closing statement
================================================================

The corpus is now a deterministic, hash-bound evidence
component. Future T-section and S-section work binds against
this hash; changing any byte of T.1-T.9 material will produce a
different corpus_hash_v1 and the binding chain will detect the
drift.
